items.reason: No server route or database function is written in these screens (items list: none). The screens reach the server only through shared code: the gym calls member_board, member_board_push, member_gym_busy, member_mate_board, member_mate_profile, member_mate_share, member_mate_stop, member_machine_busy, member_machine_push, member_trainer_status, member_trainer_share, member_trainer_stop, member_trainer_help, member_ask_choices, member_ask_trainer (anyone may run them; each takes the member's own gym key and works out the gym from it); the cloud copy (signed-in account only, acts on that account); and Find my gym's two public web addresses (start the WhatsApp number check, send a gym lead; anyone may call them, their limits sit on the server and were judged by the server areas). The QA links (qa-plan, qa-signin, qa-push, qa-dots, qa-sleep) do nothing outside a QA build.

Every gym table these screens reach has row rules on and no rule letting the apps read it, so the phone can only go through the gym-key calls above (apps cannot read the tables). Per table, the test that proves another gym is refused: leaderboard (gym_member_board, gym_board_meta) 0037_leaderboard.sql:178-180; gym mate profiles (gym_mate_profiles, gym_mate_workouts) 0040_gym_mate_profiles.sql:107-109; gym busy hours (check-ins) 0039_gym_busy.sql:124-126; trainer share (gym_trainer_members) 0050_trainer_view.sql:95 and :143; trainer questions 0053_ask_trainer_and_progress.sql:90 and :113-117; gym messages 0069_member_messages.sql:72 and :97; diet plan 0035_trainer_measurements_diet.sql:111 and :176; gym timings 0036_gym_timings.sql:67. The cloud copy is per person, not per gym: member_items lets a signed-in person read only their own rows, and 0032_member_cloud.sql:93 and :102 prove another person and the gym see none. Busy machines (gym_exercise_starts): no test, see L3.3.

Rule applied. One table has no second-gym test: busy machines. The test makes a second gym and its members but never asks the member calls with a gym B key against gym A's machines and starts. It is the same busy machines test gap already written for the owner side, so that finding is reused (its fix, a second-gym check in the busy machines test, covers the member calls too).
Rule applied: no live cross-gym attempt was made; only code, catalog rows and database test files were read. No database row was queried.
The secret search has no hit in these screen folders (items list: none). The only phone hits are the Google services file (a public app id, outside this area). Nothing in these screens holds a key.

No AI key ships in these screens. The AI coach page (switched off) only lets a member type their own provider keys, kept in the phone's secure store; Ask an AI shares a text summary to another app and calls no AI service.

These screens hold no sign-in, PIN or session of their own. Find my gym proves the number by the member sending one WhatsApp message (no code to type or guess on the phone); the proof is used once and a second use is told to start again. Code-guess limits and session length sit on the server and were judged by the server areas.

Text boxes (name, bio, link, routine names, notes, Find my gym boxes) go to the phone's own database with bound values only; column names come from fixed code lists. The profile link accepts only web (http or https) addresses, so no other kind of link can be stored and opened. Find my gym sends JSON bodies, with a length limit on each box.

No screen here uploads a file to a server: progress and workout photos stay on the phone (an optional shrunk copy goes only to Android's own backup). The one file taken in is Bring in from Hevy or Strong, which reads a member-picked spreadsheet with a library that has two known high flaws (finding reused).

The widget link that starts a workout starts by itself only with the widget's own one-time key; any other app's link gets a one-tap question. A gym mate's page is opened by a random id and the server refuses another gym (0040 test). Find my gym opens the join page with the code the server returned to that proven number; guessable join codes are a server matter already written up by the server area.

Two library flags reach these screens: the spreadsheet library 0.18.5 (two high alerts, read by the Hevy or Strong import page) and the screen-navigation library (high, every screen here). Both are already written by sibling phone areas and are reused. Gradle alerts are in the watch and a native module, not in these screens.
